key_insight: TurtLES benchmarks neural PDE surrogates on realistic 3D turbulent cylinder wakes, exposing instability and loss of small-scale energy in long-horizon predictions.
engineering_relevance: It tests whether fast CFD surrogates can handle turbulent wakes at industrially relevant mesh resolutions across geometry, Reynolds number, and angle of attack.
method: Generate turbulent wakes using high-fidelity implicit large-eddy simulations.
Represent flows on dense irregular meshes with 3–11 million points per frame.
Benchmark state-of-the-art neural operators using autoregressive rollouts.
evidence_signal: The 14 TB dataset contains 400 trajectories of 400 time steps each, with evaluations revealing temporal instability and difficulty preserving small-scale turbulent energy.
watch_item: The dataset’s scale and irregular meshes create substantial storage and computational demands for training and evaluation.
paper_title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates
